thread:
maria: Heads-up: after pushing mixed-quant rollout (FP8 primary, INT8 fallback) to dedicated-pool-7 we see eval deltas and structured JSON outputs breaking for the invoices eval set.

maria: Eval delta: accuracy -3.4%, structured-parse failures +18%. Repro steps and summary below. :frowning:

maria: Repro (quick):
```
# model config used in rollout
quant: mix_modes: [fp8, int8]
calibration_profile: online_batch
routing.policy: prefer.fp8_then_int8
batching: continuous = true, max_batch_size = 32
kv_cache: enabled = true, alignment = auto
```

maria: Example broken output (expected JSON array of line items, got partial/garbled JSON):
```json
{"invoice_id": 12345, "lines": [
  {"desc": "Widget A", "qty": 2}
  // <-- missing comma and truncated tokens
```

jonathan: :eyes: Do you have the kernel selection trace from the runtime? could be a kernel boundary/serialization bug when we switch kernels mid-sequence.

maria: attaching sample logs below (trimmed):
```
[2026-07-12T18:03:22Z] request id=rpc-8fa3, model=rw-mix-v2, seq_len=512, picked_kernel=fp8_fused_attn, kv_cache_hit=true
[2026-07-12T18:03:22Z] request id=rpc-8fa3, switched_kernel=int8_attn_small_seq, kv_cache_rebase=true
[2026-07-12T18:03:22Z] request id=rpc-8fa3, emit tokens: "{\"invoice_id\": 12345, \"lines\": ["
```

raj: This smells like KV cache key alignment + kernel switching. If the fp8 path writes KV in one layout and int8 expects another, the decoder stream could get corrupted when we fall back mid-request. We saw something similar with attention-pad offsets earlier.

kelly: I ran a micro-profiling pass on dedicated-pool-7 for the same request stream: perf-bot results below. Notable: fp8 kernels are ~1.9x faster but we see a ~7% tokenization/emit stall when kernel switch occurs.

perf-bot: Benchmark snippet:
```
scenario: invoices-eval
avg_latency_fp8_only: 42ms
avg_latency_int8_only: 88ms
avg_latency_mixed (switch events): 55ms
kernel_switch_penalty_est: ~12ms per switch
```

sophie: Could also be calibration mismatch: the online_batch calibration_profile can produce slightly different quant scales per batch; if batches cross request boundaries due to continuous batching, the same KV entries might get compressed differently. That would corrupt subsequent attention reads.

jonathan: Can we reproduce deterministically in a unit test? maybe force a mid-sequence kernel switch in the runtime with a synthetic stream and assert structured outputs match fp32 baseline.

maria: I created a minimal repro harness (attached to the thread in the ticket): synthetic stream that toggles routing.policy every N tokens. It reproduces 95% of the time locally.

maria: Quick mitigation: rollback routing.policy to fp8_prefer_no_switch for the affected pool; this reduces structured failures to baseline but increases cost ~25%. Need decision for rollout.

kelly: For triage:
- hypothesis A: KV layout mismatch between fp8 and int8 kernels when kv_cache_rebase=true
- hypothesis B: calibration-induced value drift leading to token misprediction cascade
- hypothesis C: batching heuristics cause partial-batch calibration mix across requests

raj: Triage steps I propose:
1) Add assert checks in KV serializer to validate checksum after kernel switch. Fail fast to capture binary diff.
2) Add a unit test that forces kernel_switch mid-request with the invoices eval prompt set.
3) Run a narrow A/B on dedicated-pool-7 with routing.policy=fp8_only vs fp8_prefer_no_switch for 1k requests and compare structured-parse rate.

sophie: I'll take (2) and (3). jonathan, can you add (1) or point me to where the kv serializer lives?

jonathan: I'll drop a patch to insert a simple CRC32 header in KV stores and a validation check on read. If checksum mismatch -> log full dump to s3 and switch to safe-fallback-mode (spill to fp32).

ci-bot: quick test run on CI: invoices-eval smoke (n=120): fp8_only pass_rate=82%, mixed-rollout pass_rate=67%, int8_only pass_rate=80%. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/tmp/invoices-1891234567/

maria: Thanks. Let's prioritize checksum + test. If we can catch corruption and auto-fallback to fp32/int8 we get safety and time to fully root cause.

kelly: Also recommend adding telemetry counters for kernel_switch_count per request and percent of requests that experienced kv_cache_rebase after a switch. Fill an observability dashboard.

raj: I'll own the KV checksum PR; will include a small compatibility shim so existing caches don't fail immediately (rotate on read). ETA end of day.

sophie: I'll run the A/B later today and post the numbers. If mixed still fails we should revert the rollout for infra safety.

maria: ok plan: rollback routing.policy for pool in 1 hour if we don't have a crashing repro + checksum landing. Will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: if we lock to fp8_only we should expect ~20-30% cost delta; communicate to finance if rollback goes >24h.

jonathan: filed tracking issue infra#4521 with links to s3 artifacts and CI results.

maria: Appreciate the quick responses. will follow up with artifacts and the repro harness link in infra#4521.

sophie: Posted A/B results: fp8_only pass=91/120, mixed pass=78/120. Recommending rollback now.

maria: Rolling back routing.policy on dedicated-pool-7 to fp8_prefer_no_switch. Will monitor.

raj: monitoring hooks added: kv_checksum_mismatch_count, kernel_switch_per_request.

jonathan: landed CRC32 KV check in staging branch, tests added.

maria: closing loop when monitoring shows stable. thanks all. :rocket:
